title: LaRA-Fusion: Latent-Robust Adaptation via Dual-Loop Constraints for Infrared and Visible Image Fusion
claim: Prior single-loop constraints (self-reconstruction, cycle-translation) leave latent manifolds unconstrained; our dual-loop regularization aligns manifolds across modalities, content and attributes.
layout: 3 panels: (a),(b) top-left, (c) wide bottom; dashed dividers, shared legend on top
description: A two-row legend sits at the top. It defines blue and red circles as source visible and infrared images, lighter circles as pseudo images, grey circles as a content anchor, stars as attribute codes, and purple circles as fused images. It also defines dashed manifold boundaries, a discriminator, a generic generator G_theta, and encoder/decoder trapezoids. The top row has (a) Self-reconstruction and (b) Cycle-translation. Each shows clusters of dots inside dashed boundaries, with generator arrows and an epsilon gap marking a mismatch between manifolds. The bottom row, (c) Dual-Loop Manifold Regularization, has three numbered stages. Stage 1 uses encoders to split each modality into grey content clusters and star attribute clusters. Stage 2 uses decoders, a discriminator and L_rec/L_cyc losses to reconstruct and translate. Stage 3 uses a decoder with alpha mixing and a discriminator to produce purple fused images. Brown arrows carry the flow. The eye goes first to the colorful dot clusters.
caption: Latent Robustness via Manifold Regularization. (a)
abstract: Infrared and visible image fusion (IVIF) aims to synergize complementary thermal radiation and textural details for comprehensive scene perception. However, existing unsupervised paradigms often overlook the intrinsic topological consistency shared across modalities. Lacking explicit geometric regularization, encoders frequently succumb to degenerate numerical shortcuts, capturing superficial high-frequency noise rather than domain-invariant semantic structures to satisfy reconstruction objectives. To address this, we propose LaRA-Fusion, a framework achieving Latent-Robust Adaptation via Dual-Loop Manifold Constraints. We construct a strictly constrained latent space where an inner loop enforces geometric reversibility, while an outer loop aligns the generated representations with the target data distribution. This mechanism effectively mitigates latent space collapse, compelling the model to extract topologically aligned features that remain robust against modality-specific variations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LaRA-Fusion outperforms state-of-the-art methods with superior robustness and interpretability.
